title: Sobolev lifting bounds for C^(d-1),1 curves in finite complex invariant quotients with maximal generator degree d at least two
author: Adam Parusiński; Armin Rainer
difficulty_reason: The proof repeatedly normalizes the largest invariant radical and reduces the curve to a smaller stabilizer while keeping derivative estimates uniform. Its group-order induction controls lifts on specially prepared subintervals, and a multiplicity-two cover glues those bounds across the singular zero set. The final bound tracks distinct generator degrees and the full interval length, producing the strict p<d/(d-1) range without assuming a polynomial or coregular quotient.
source_version: Official SIGMA 17 (2021) article 037, DOI 10.3842/SIGMA.2021.037; journal PDF and native TeX acquired 2026-09-30, exact bytes pinned by SHA256

proof_review.method: Published author proof/core and local context fidelity screening
proof_review.note: Complete author Theorem1.1 proof is supplied, including uniform Luna slice reduction, all new local derivative estimates, reduced-admissible induction8.2 and the two global interval cases. Select a finite group representation on a finite-dimensional complex V with a minimal homogeneous basic-invariant system sigma_j of degrees d_j and maximal degree d>=2. The curve on a bounded open interval extends with C^(d-1),1 coordinate regularity to its closure and takes values in sigma(V); every continuous lift is absolutely continuous with the exact1.1 Lp derivative bound for1<=p<d/(d-1). The constant depends on the representation, chosen invariants, interval length and p; endpoint-independent strengthening and the critical weak-Lp question are not claimed. Prior radical derivative bounds, Luna slices, interpolation and prepared-cover theorem are identified source background. The source elementary slice-degree observation4.5 points to the existing polynomial-generator/Taylor-minimality argument, explicitly written as Lemma3 on physical page12 of prior arXiv1406.2485v3; this was checked for the cited dependency scope, not reproduced or independently rederived. The full new group-order lifting induction and gluing core is written in this article. Multivariable and Q-valued variants are not separately counted.
